title: Carousel Momentum & Fluid Conservation Lab
description: A horse figurine is mounted on a spinning turntable alongside a coffee mug filled with simulated liquid. The user adjusts the turntable's angular velocity, tilts the platform, adds or removes mass tokens onto the horse and mug, and observes how angular momentum conservation and fluid level equilibrium respond. An undo/redo system tracks every parameter change across 10+ interaction steps.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load coffeeMug.glb and horse.glb, scaling both to roughly 1 unit tall. Place them on a circular turntable platform (a flat cylinder, radius 3, height 0.15) centered at the origin. Position the horse at offset (1, 0.15, 0) and the mug at (-1, 0.15, 0) on the platform. Fill the mug with a translucent blue cylinder representing liquid whose height varies with centrifugal effects. Camera starts at (0, 5, 8) looking at origin. Add ambient light intensity 0.6 and a directional light from (5, 10, 5). Build a left-side HTML control panel with: (1) a slider for angular velocity (-10 to 10 rad/s), (2) a slider for platform tilt angle (-15 to 15 degrees around X-axis), (3) buttons to add/remove brass mass tokens (small gold torus meshes) that snap onto the horse or mug when clicked, (4) a toggle to lock/unlock the mug position radially on the platform, (5) Undo and Redo buttons. Each frame, rotate the turntable group by angular velocity times delta-time. Compute effective moment of inertia from base platform plus each mass token at its radial distance squared. Display conserved angular momentum L = I * omega in a top HUD. When the user changes mass distribution, auto-adjust omega to conserve L, clamped to safe bounds. Simulate liquid height in the mug as a function of omega squared and tilt angle using a simplified parabolic surface model: raise the liquid mesh on the outer edge and lower it on the inner edge. Tilt the entire turntable group around X by the tilt slider value. Mass tokens are placed by clicking the horse or mug; a raycaster determines which object receives the token. Store every slider change, token add/remove, lock toggle, and tilt change as a state snapshot in an undo stack (max 30). Undo restores the previous snapshot; Redo re-applies. Show a step counter indicating how many interactions have been performed. The task requires at least 10 steps: set velocity, add 2 tokens to horse, add 2 tokens to mug, tilt platform, adjust velocity again, lock mug, remove a token, undo twice, redo once. Render at 60fps with a subtle grid floor below the turntable for spatial reference.
